question.problem: Find the intersection of intervals $(-2,\infty )\cap (1,\infty ).$ Express the result as an inequality.
question.worked_solution:
We start by sketching the two intervals $(-2,\infty )$ and $(1,\infty )$ separately:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14248994/assets/4bd70e5f89643a5d2b19954003435b4c6aeec24c68bb3cd1f6a4e7a98c14f847.png)

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14248994/assets/eff58d0bb2d496d608ae1e415f38589c5b9b13efe1f282d172fb5313ba6792ff.png)

The intersection $(-2,\infty )\cap (1,\infty )$ represents the values that are in both intervals. So, it can be graphed by finding where the two intervals overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14248994/assets/6131e16f37e8ec44eae8c085be60a28dd094390e1975bdafe256cdc9e229f3dc.png)

Thus, $(-2,\infty )\cap (1,\infty )=(1,\infty ).$ This corresponds to the inequality $x>1.$
